revisions.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Redesign the referenced molecular-puzzle logo according to the user's new concept. Keep the same polished rounded 3D enamel style, deep petrol teal / pale mint / warm peach palette, soft highlights, open molecular silhouette and genuine transparent background. NEW SUBJECT: three separate chemically coherent BALL-AND-STICK fragments CH3, CH2 and OH, aligned and hovering close to one another as if about to join into ETHANOL, CH3-CH2-OH. LEFT FRAGMENT CH3: exactly one teal carbon sphere with three attached smaller mint hydrogen spheres, and one short open carbon-carbon bond stem pointing toward the center. MIDDLE FRAGMENT CH2: exactly one teal carbon sphere with two attached smaller mint hydrogen spheres, an open C-C half-bond facing the left fragment and an open C-O half-bond facing the right fragment. RIGHT FRAGMENT OH: exactly one warm peach oxygen sphere with one attached smaller mint hydrogen sphere and an open O-C half-bond facing the middle carbon fragment. Total visible atoms across the three groups: exactly TWO teal carbons, SIX mint hydrogens, ONE peach oxygen. All hydrogens belong to the stated fragment: three on first carbon, two on second carbon, one on oxygen. Maintain a plausible 3D ethanol arrangement: tetrahedral bond directions around each carbon with clear near/far depth; bent geometry at oxygen. The fragments should be visibly separated only by small transparent gaps along the two inter-group bond directions. Put matching rounded jigsaw tab/socket connectors ONLY on the cut bond ends at the C-C and C-O gaps, making it clear that the three molecular groups will click together into ethanol. ABSOLUTELY NO jigsaw seams, puzzle lines, cuts or grooves on any atom sphere. Atom surfaces must be smooth seamless spheres. Do not place molecular groups on flat tiles or blocks. Use a compact slightly bent composition and an oblique three-quarter view so all three fragments are distinct and readable as one molecule being assembled; fully frame every atom and connector with transparent margins. No extra atoms, no puzzle seams on atoms, no letters or chemical labels, no text, no numbers, no rectangular board, no hands, no glow or haze, no backdrop, no pedestal, no watermark.

revisions.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Completely replace the ball-and-stick molecular rendering with the user's much simpler TWO-DIMENSIONAL logo concept: exactly THREE flat jigsaw puzzle tiles that represent the three groups of ethanol, coming together left-to-right. Keep only the Namelecule family palette from the reference: pale mint, deep petrol teal and warm pale peach. LEFT TILE pale mint, exact centered bold dark-teal text 'CH₃' (3 must be a proper smaller subscript). MIDDLE TILE deep petrol teal, exact centered bold pale-mint text 'CH₂' (2 must be a proper smaller subscript). RIGHT TILE warm pale peach, exact centered bold dark-teal text 'OH'. The text must be clear, large and correctly spelled: CH₃, CH₂, OH. Make all three outlines unmistakably jigsaw-puzzle pieces with matching rounded tabs and sockets at their facing left/right sides. The three tiles are almost joined, with small clean transparent gaps that show how they connect; the right OH tile is slightly lifted toward its final position, with at most a very slight rotation so its text stays highly legible. The two links between the groups can include thin dark-teal single-bond strokes aligned through the connectors, so when joined the result reads CH₃—CH₂—OH. Use a clean polished flat 2D vector-like illustration, solid colors, gentle rounded corners, balanced compact horizontal composition and generous transparent margins. No 3D extrusion, perspective, glossy spheres, atom balls, ball-and-stick rods, shadows or gradients. No extra pieces or extra atoms. No word ethanol, title, caption, watermark, hands, rectangular background board, border, or backdrop. Actual transparent background. The three puzzle pieces themselves are the entire logo.
